goal: Implement configured OIDC identity, secure PostgreSQL sessions and consistent catalog access; reserve real issuer/staging verification for release acceptance.
acceptance_tests: The provider-neutral deployment identity contract and R4 session handoff are documented before implementation; actual issuer/client/origin registration remains a separate live-acceptance prerequisite.
Production rejects invalid or development-only credentials and enforces configured roles and scope.
Source, canonical, processing-state and media access obey the same policy.
Credential values never enter browser bundles, logs, tracked configuration or evidence.
Independent deterministic security verification is required; actual staging identities are additionally required before production verification, with sensitive reporting following SECURITY.md.

OIDC code/PKCE and server-side sessions pass deterministic issuer and real-PostgreSQL tests; Workshop consumes the committed same-origin session contract, with live issuer verification recorded separately.
OIDC startup requires a working PostgreSQL pool and migrated auth tables; it never falls back to memory persistence.
Explicit local mode retains headless bearer clients only; Workshop session login requires configured OIDC, including development.

The shared driver accepts exactly001–039, audits039 as a complete transaction at all four dispatch sites, rejects untracked auth-only baselines and preserves all historical001–038 bytes and prefix regressions.

The private fixture collector executes five mandatory real PostgreSQL Go session subtests, rejects missing dependencies/configuration and all skips, and records exact039 migration and candidate provenance using the independently verified R3 image/service.
forbidden_scope: Changing the autonomy policy or weakening required checks
Publishing secrets or private source payloads
Editing paths outside the assigned scope
Changing the requested gpt-6.1-sol / medium / Fast execution profile or silently falling back to another model or tier

compatibility.api: Preserve existing consumers with additive versioned fields; run compatibility checks.
compatibility.events: Preserve event identity and make duplicate delivery idempotent.
compatibility.schema: Forward-only additive migrations with clean and upgrade verification; no destructive edits to historical migrations.
